sections.title: Front matter

summary.text: The front matter of the report of the 8th National Tuberculosis Programme Managers Meeting and 13th Wolfheze Workshop, held in The Hague in June 2008 and organized by WHO Europe, KNCV and ECDC. It includes an abstract on drug-resistant TB and TB/HIV in the WHO European Region and the eighteen high-priority countries, keywords and a table of contents listing sessions and annexes. The abstract notes the meeting's focus on management, surveillance and evaluation of TB control.

sections.title: Executive summary

summary.text: Summarizes the Wolfheze 2008 meeting, starting from the Berlin Ministerial Forum on TB in 2007 and the four mechanisms for turning its commitments into action, including the Stop TB Strategy and regional and EU plans. It reports discussions on follow-up of the Berlin Declaration, scaling up responses to multidrug-resistant TB, TB in migrants and rapid diagnostics. It ends with agreement that a review of TB elimination like that done for the Netherlands would be useful in other low-incidence countries, with ECDC and WHO involvement.

sections.extract: The Ministerial Forum on TB was organized on 22 October 2007 in Berlin, Germany. It expressed the political commitment of all Member States to fight TB and address the threat of multidrug-resistant (MDR-) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR-) TB in the WHO European Region – the highest rates in the world. Four mechanisms are available to translate the commitment taken in Berlin into action: • the Global Plan to Stop

sections.title: Introduction

summary.text: Introduces the Wolfheze workshops, an annual meeting series begun in 1990 by the Dutch Tuberculosis Foundation for TB programme managers in low-prevalence western European countries, and their expansion with WHO and partner support. It explains that the 2008 event combined the NTP managers meeting with the workshop and that the surveillance correspondents meeting is reported separately.

sections.extract: Wolfheze is a workshop and a movement named after a small village near Arnhem in the Netherlands, where in 1990 Koninklijke Nederlandse Centrale Vereniging tot bestrijding der tuberculose (KNCV – Dutch Tuberculosis (TB) Foundation) organized the first workshop for national TB programme (NTP) managers of low-TB-prevalence countries in western Europe. sections.title: Objectives of the meeting

summary.text: Sets out the objectives of the 2008 meeting, including reviewing the Berlin Declaration as an advocacy tool and the plan to stop TB in 18 high-priority European countries, in the context of the Millennium Development Goal targets. It also states the aim of the surveillance correspondents meeting to understand new regional coordination arrangements.

sections.extract: Wolfheze 2008 represented an excellent opportunity to have an extended forum for discussion on the challenges and opportunities shared by all countries in the Region to further the work to meet the targets of Millennium Development Goal 6, by the year 2015, through preventing multidrug-resistant (MDR-) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR-) TB. sections.title: Opening session

summary.text: Reports the opening session of Wolfheze 2008, with its programme of speakers on welcome, the Stop TB ambassador's address, the purpose of the workshops and the future of TB surveillance in Europe. It summarizes remarks on the history of the Wolfheze movement and the importance of surveillance in regional and EU TB control plans.

sections.title: Plenary session 1: Follow-up on the Berlin Declaration on TB

summary.text: Reports the first plenary session on follow-up to the Berlin Declaration on TB, listing speakers from WHO Europe, ECDC and KNCV and interventions from programme managers. It describes the proposed framework and process for monitoring countries' commitments. Conclusions stress involving all stakeholders, accurate two-way flow of information, feasible indicators and attention to country conditions.

sections.title: Plenary session 2: Strategic plans for TB high-priority countries and for the European Union

summary.text: Reports the second plenary on strategic plans for the 18 high-priority TB countries in the WHO European Region and the EU Framework Action Plan, including partner assistance to countries. It outlines the main directions of each plan and the discussion that followed. Conclusions call for adapting plans to country settings and for TB programme managers to engage in health reforms so TB services reach primary care.

sections.title: Plenary session 3: TB control in migrants

summary.text: Reports the plenary session on TB control in migrants, covering ECDC work on migrant health and TB screening, experience in the Russian Federation and TB among undocumented persons in France. It summarizes the evidence and discussion on screening approaches. Conclusions favour access to free diagnosis and treatment for undocumented people and screening policies that do not harm migrants.

sections.title: Plenary session 4: Role of rapid detection for drug-resistant TB

summary.text: Reports the plenary on rapid detection of drug-resistant TB, with presentations on available methods and FIND demonstration projects, and steps for country implementation. It notes that molecular line-probe assays are easy to implement where molecular testing exists, with attention to temperature control, training and quality control.

sections.title: Parallel session 1: How can MDR-TB interventions be scaled up in the 18 TB high- priority countries in the WHO European Region?

summary.text: Reports a parallel session on scaling up MDR-TB interventions in the 18 high-priority European countries, held in Russian- and English-speaking groups. Its recommendations include motivating, training and supervising health staff, and supervision of national TB programmes by WHO and other international partners.

sections.title: Parallel session 2: Discussion on the draft document ‘TB contact investigation in low-prevalence countries’

summary.text: Reports a Wolfheze 2008 parallel session on a draft consensus document on TB contact investigation in low- and intermediate-incidence countries, giving the chairs and agenda. It explains that KNCV initiated the document following the 2006 Wolfheze Workshop, and summarises working-group discussion on definitions, priority contacts, outbreak management and research needs. It closes with agreed next steps, including a deadline for comments and the membership of the writing group.

sections.title: Parallel session 3: Scaling up TB/HIV interventions in the European Region

summary.text: Reports the parallel session on scaling up joint TB/HIV interventions in the WHO European Region, listing the agenda and the main obstacles raised, such as poor coordination between programmes, missing co-infection data and separate services. It ends with recommendations including legislative support, civil society involvement, infection control and a regional workshop.

sections.title: Parallel session 4: Guidelines for TB infection control in the European Region

summary.text: Reports the parallel session on regional guidelines for TB infection control, explaining their origin in rising MDR-TB in eastern Europe and the actions WHO Europe has already taken, such as a training course in Bucharest. Recommendations set a deadline for final comments and call on countries to draw up national infection control plans.

sections.title: Parallel session 5: (How) can country reviews contribute to TB control in a low- incidence country?

summary.text: Reports the parallel session on whether external reviews of national TB programmes help low-incidence countries, with presentations on the Netherlands review and ECDC plans for country visits. It recommends that WHO and ECDC take part in reviews, which should become best practice and be carried out by trained, mixed teams.

sections.title: Parallel session 6: TB control strengthening health systems

summary.text: Reports the parallel session on how TB control can contribute to health system strengthening, including human resource development and Global Fund opportunities. Country experiences from Lithuania, Latvia, Kyrgyzstan, Israel and others are noted, followed by recommendations that TB programmes engage with health sector reform.

sections.title: Closure

summary.text: Summarises the closing session of the Wolfheze 2008 workshops, with conclusions presented separately for low/intermediate- and high-incidence countries. For low-incidence settings it covers contact investigation definitions, TB among immigrants, rapid MDR-TB tests and programme reviews. It ends by noting the value of country reviews for awareness, political commitment and programme effectiveness whatever the local epidemiology.
